solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drug arrest takes place behind prison

indicators.note: the arrest-and-takes-place pieces come after the prison piece, sitting behind it

parts.note: can is slang for a prison or jail
to nab someone is to arrest them
something that is, exists or happens, so 'takes place' gives is

explanation.surface: A drug bust happens just outside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is a well-known recreational narcotic, so it is a straightforward example of a drug.

clue.text: News agency journal's not the first where things are kept buzzing?

parts.note: AP is the Associated Press, a news agency

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the journal word is dropped

parts.note: a diary is a journal; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A press agency's journal is missing its first page, in a place where things are hectic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees, which buzz, are kept in a beehouse or hive collection, so the cryptic phrase describes a bee yard.

clue.text: Language of Nag's Head replacing that of its general classification

indicators.note: the head of Nag takes the place of the head of the classification word

parts.note: a nag belongs to the broad category of horse

indicators.note: the head of the word Nag is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pub called the Nag's Head speaks some language connected with its category.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nag's Head is a common British pub name, which hides the real instruction: swap the first letter of the general word for a nag with the first letter of Nag.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the tongue of the medieval Scandinavians and Vikings.

clue.text: Contentious because shielded by corporations mostly

indicators.note: the because piece sits inside, protected by the trimmed bellies
says the last letter of the corporations word is left off

parts.note: corporation is a jocular word for a pot belly, so corporations are bellies
'cos is an informal shortening of because

explanation.surface: Something is controversial because big companies are protecting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose means aggressive and eager to fight, close in sense to quarrelsome or argumentative.

clue.text: Droopy person perhaps accepting wife's arrogance

indicators.note: the droopy word takes the wife letter into itself

parts.note: something that sags or droops could be called a sagger
W is the standard abbreviation for wife; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A sagging, droopy figure takes on his wife's haughty manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Swagger is a boastful, conceited strut or manner, which is a show of arrogance.

clue.text: Stage of travel in package almost makes Indian disaster zone

indicators.note: the travel stage goes inside the shortened package word
says the package word loses its final letter

parts.note: a bale is a bundled package of goods
a hop is one short leg of a journey, especially a flight

explanation.surface: A leg of a trip in a holiday package nearly turns into a disaster area in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city suffered the 1984 Union Carbide gas leak, one of the worst industrial catastrophes ever.

clue.text: Tough is only approximately hard

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
c is short for circa, meaning approximately
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Something is only roughly difficult, not truly tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch describes someone robustly masculine and rugged in appearance or manner.

clue.text: No day ever worked to save time for cook

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters have been kneaded or manipulated into a new shape

explanation.surface: A cook who never has a day off would welcome shortcuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Supermarket food sold ready for the oven is prepared in advance so a cook can skip the preparation work.

clue.text: Softened when core of satsuma's ripened

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the core is the central pair of letters in the fruit word with its 's

parts.note: aged means matured or ripened, like cheese

explanation.surface: A satsuma's centre grew soft once it ripened.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage pain or anger is to ease or soothe it, so the past form means eased or mitigated.

clue.text: I run repeatedly through litigation over peninsula

indicators.note: I and the doubled run letter pass through the middle of the reversed litigation word
in a down-or-across sense over signals the litigation word turned back to front

parts.note: law, as in going to law, means litigation

indicators.note: the run letter appears twice in succession

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone keeps campaigning through court cases about a stretch of coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns LAW into WAL; IRR then goes through it. The Wirral is a peninsula in north-west England between the Dee and Mersey estuaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wirral is a named English headland region bounded by two estuaries and the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Seen to try cases with theatricality

indicators.note: something that has been seen to has been dealt with or fixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge has been observed hearing trials in a showy, dramatic style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen to' looks like a verb phrase about a judge but signals rearranging TRY and CASES.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal adjective describes behaviour that is affected and showy, like a stage performer's mannerisms.

clue.text: Bitter and spirit at no cost

parts.note: free means costing nothing
zing is liveliness or vigour, a sense of spirit

explanation.surface: A bitter beer and a drink of spirits come gratis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' and 'spirit' suggest drinks at a bar, but bitter here means intensely cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter weather is sharply, painfully cold, the same idea as icy chill.

clue.text: Brother relapses, covered in salve derived from plants

indicators.note: the reversed brother piece is wrapped by the salve word

parts.note: to salve a wound is to heal it

indicators.note: relapses suggests falling back, so the brother abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A sick monk falls ill again and gets smothered in ointment made from plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedies or teas made from herbs are botanical, coming from leaves, roots and flowers.

clue.text: One supervising Sellers in Goon realm, far gone

indicators.note: gone in the sense of crazy or wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Peter Sellers of The Goon Show is overseen in a far-off zany kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Sellers with its capital points to Peter Sellers, star of The Goon Show, a classic BBC radio comedy; really it means shop staff who sell.
explanation.definitionFit: In a department store the person in charge of one level oversees the sales staff working there.

clue.text: Penning Chapter One, enjoyable French writer means to combat smut?

parts.note: something fun is enjoyable

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the French writer holds the chapter and one letters

parts.note: Andre Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A French author writes a fun first chapter as a weapon against obscenity.
explanation.walkthrough: Smut looks like pornography, but it is also a fungal disease of cereal crops, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical spray that kills fungi is used by farmers against crop blights such as smut and rust.

clue.text: To naturals, playing needs no intro from Louis Armstrong, say

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around freely to form a new word
the intro of Louis is its first letter, which the anagram must do without

explanation.surface: Natural talents are performing without needing an introduction to the jazz great Louis Armstrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis Armstrong seems a single name, but 'Louis' only supplies L, which 'needs no' removes from TO NATURALS before 'playing' rearranges the rest; Armstrong alone points to Neil.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong, the first man on the Moon, was a famous space traveller; 'say' marks him as one example.

clue.text: No countryman's right to veto, stopping completely without question

indicators.note: the right and veto pieces plug the gap inside the trimmed word, stopping it like a cork
the question letter is removed from the completely word

parts.note: quite can mean completely, as in 'quite right'
to ban something is to veto or forbid it

explanation.surface: A rural man has every right to block something, wholly without debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A city dweller is the opposite of a rustic, so is not a person of the countryside.

clue.text: Embarrassing once second person's after call to have debts turned into credit

indicators.note: the archaic possessive comes after the rest
the call and reversed debts pieces are put into the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: the debts word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: to owe is to have debts
thy is the archaic possessive of the second person singular

explanation.surface: A borrower phones up hoping their debts will be magically converted into credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the second-person possessive as archaic, the old form used before 'your' took over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so awkward it makes you wince or cringe is highly embarrassing to witness.

clue.text: Dead person's content to welcome the man at edge of Underworld — such as me?

indicators.note: the inner letters take in the man and the edge piece
the content of the word is what lies inside its outer letters, so both ends are dropped

parts.note: a corpse is a dead person; the 's is possessive
he is the pronoun for the man

indicators.note: the edge of Underworld is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dead soul is happy to greet a visitor arriving at the threshold of Hades.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks in the voice of the mythical singer who went down to Hades to fetch Eurydice and reached its edge; the question mark flags that the definition is the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Thracian musician famously journeyed to the Greek realm of the dead, so the clue makes him its narrator.

clue.text: Dust fills something like strut (for a glider)

indicators.note: the dust word fills the gap inside the for-example word

parts.note: say means for example, introducing something like what follows
ash is powdery dust left after burning

explanation.surface: Dust gets into a support strut on a glider plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strut' looks like a structural brace in a glider's frame, but it is a verb, and the glider is someone who moves smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in a gliding, swaggering, showy way, a strut done smoothly.

clue.text: Unhinged mother rejected first son

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: rejected suggests being turned back, so the son's name is reversed

parts.note: in Genesis Cain was the first son of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A deranged mother disowns her eldest boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A madman is someone wildly deranged, so the noun can stand as an adjective meaning crazed.

clue.text: Heap in car crashes

indicators.note: a crash scrambles a car, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clapped-out old banger keeps crashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a mound of stones piled up as a landmark or memorial.

clue.text: Encourage It Girl to dismiss time waster

parts.note: to prod someone is to urge or encourage them

indicators.note: the time letter is sent away from the It and girl pieces

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone urges a glamorous socialite to sack a time-waster.
explanation.walkthrough: An It Girl is a young socialite much in the gossip columns; here 'It' and 'Girl' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift who squanders money, like the son in the parable, is a wasteful person.

clue.text: Commitment to avoid tricks after master leaves French department

indicators.note: the master letter departs from the bid word

parts.note: misere in card games such as solo whist is a bid undertaking to win no tricks

explanation.surface: A promise to stop playing pranks once the teacher has gone, in some part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricks' looks like pranks, but it means the tricks won at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isere is an administrative region of south-eastern France, named after its river.

clue.text: M goes over peak with one off-road vehicle

indicators.note: the letter word spreads over and encloses the one and peak pieces

parts.note: Mike is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter M
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nib is a point or tip, a peak in that sense

explanation.surface: A rider called M crests a summit on an all-terrain machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A small motorcycle built for rough tracks is used for off-road riding.

clue.text: Soul singer informally appearing in cabaret hall

indicators.note: says the answer appears inside the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A soul singer turns up casually performing at a cabaret venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Aretha Franklin, the Queen of Soul, is usually known by her first name, the casual form.

clue.text: Humble revolutionary entitled to hold office in the end

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the office letter inside it
a revolution turns something round, so the entitled word is reversed

parts.note: named means called or entitled

indicators.note: the final letter of office is used

explanation.surface: A humble rebel ultimately takes up a government post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' makes DEMAN from NAMED; it holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade them or bring them low, as humble does as a verb.

clue.text: Fine art sellers note article purchase's less refined

parts.note: so (soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
the is the definite article

indicators.note: the refined letter is taken away from the purchase word

parts.note: buys means purchases, with 's read as a plural
U stands for upper-class, hence refined

explanation.surface: A dealer notes that one article's purchase is rather crude.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class, refined, is a British convention from the 'U and non-U' usage debate.
explanation.definitionFit: The London auction house is a famous dealer in paintings, antiques and other fine art.
